title: fix(service-analytics): lower a dateRange preset in runCompare instead of refusing it as an invalid date
body:
Fixes #17973

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`DatasetExecutor.runCompare` read the STRING arm of `dateRange` as `[range, range]` — the degenerate fallback PR #17015 removed from every other analytics face. `parseUTC` was handed the preset NAME, so a declared, honoured member of the closed vocabulary was refused outright.

**Reproduced first**, driven through the real executor on `b3b43b6ea` (the card's `2c87a48f` line numbers had moved; the shape had not — the degenerate arm was at `:1318`):

```
### PRESET last_30_days + compareTo
### threw: Error code=DATASET_INVALID status=400 msg=[dataset-executor] invalid date in dateRange: "last_30_days"
### CONTROL explicit window -> [[["2026-01-01","2026-01-31"]],[["2025-12-01","2025-12-31"]]]
### CONTROL bogus string threw: code=DATASET_INVALID status=400
```

The severity is the FALSE diagnostic. `last_30_days` is exactly what the schema, the dashboard date filter and the docs tell an author to write, so "invalid date" sends them to check a date that is already correct — a repair that does not exist.

## What changed

Both arms now go through one face lowering, `lowerDatasetCompareDateRange`, which calls the shared `resolveAnalyticsDateRangeString` for the string arm — the same call the ObjectQL strategy, the native-SQL strategy, the draft-preview evaluator and driver-memory's cube face make. ⛔ No fourth spelling of the lowering was invented.

The resolved window is then projected onto the comparison math's UTC calendar by `inclusiveUtcDayWindow`, because `shiftRange` measures `previousPeriod` as whole days between two day-starts and `alignedCompareBucketKey` reads the upper bound as the LAST bucket. `endExclusive` is load-bearing there: the ten calendar presets report the first instant AFTER the window, so reading their bound as inclusive would make every one of them a day too long.

That split — report the window the vocabulary resolved, keep the per-face calendar translation downstream — is the one `lowerPreviewDateRange` already makes when it leaves the bare-day widening in its own predicate.

Timezone precedence is `buildQuery`'s, verbatim (`selection.timezone` then `context.timezone` then `UTC`), so the comparison window resolves in the same calendar as the primary pass it is compared against.

**The array arm is untouched, bound for bound.**

After:

```
### PRESET last_30_days + compareTo
### threw: NOTHING
### windows: [["last_30_days"],[["2026-07-16","2026-08-15"]]]
### CONTROL explicit window -> [[["2026-01-01","2026-01-31"]],[["2025-12-01","2025-12-31"]]]   (byte-identical)
### CONTROL bogus string threw: code=ANALYTICS_DATE_RANGE_UNRECOGNIZED status=400
```

`runCompare` is also registered as the fourth face in the shared conformance kit, as the card asks.

## ⚠️ One consequence worth reviewing

On this path an out-of-vocabulary `dateRange` STRING used to answer `DATASET_INVALID`; it now answers the ADR-0112 `ANALYTICS_DATE_RANGE_UNRECOGNIZED` / 400 envelope the other four faces already raise. One condition, one envelope. The changeset states it as a consumer-facing note. The `DATASET_INVALID "invalid date in dateRange"` refusal for an ARRAY bound that is not a date is unchanged.

## Pins

The card asks for a pin that asserts the preset **lowers-and-shifts**, not merely that the string changed. Five cases, driven end to end through `DatasetExecutor.execute`, expectations stated literally against the frozen clock and only cross-checked against the shared resolver — ⛔ never computed with `shiftRange`, which would restate the implementation and pass for any window at all:

- a CALENDAR preset lowers with its exclusive end honoured (September stops on the 30th, not October 1st) and shifts a year back;
- a ROLLING preset reaches NOW's own day and `previousPeriod` shifts by the window's own length;
- five distinct presets select five DISTINCT comparison windows (the fallback's real signature was twelve of thirteen names collapsing onto one);
- an unrecognised string is refused on the ENVELOPE, not on `toThrow()` — this face DID throw before the fix;
- CONTROL: the caller's explicit window is still shifted bound for bound.

⛔ No existing test pinned the defect as setup, so none was repaired, skipped or weakened. The two fixtures that assert `invalid date in dateRange` (`packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-unlisted-refusal-envelope.test.ts:186` and `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/unlisted-refusal-envelope.test.ts:264`) both drive the ARRAY arm and are unaffected — measured, not assumed.

## Reverse verification

The fix was committed first, then mutated back out on disk.

- Mutation landed: anchor `inclusiveUtcDayWindow(lowered)` 1 to 0, degenerate `[td.dateRange as string, td.dateRange as string]` 0 to 1; blob `e0f74df` to `99f8cfb`.
- ⛔ Deliberately NOT rebuilt: the conformance test imports `../dataset-executor.js` by relative specifier, so vitest reads SOURCE. Going red without a build is itself the proof of that resolution path — a dist-resolved test would have stayed falsely green.
- Result: **4 failed, 32 passed**, and the four are exactly the four wiring controls.
- ⭐ The direction is the interesting half. The conformance-kit face registration stayed GREEN, because `lowerDatasetCompareDateRange` itself was untouched — which is precisely the "an exported helper conforms while the live path keeps its old fallback" gap, and precisely why the end-to-end block exists. The array-arm control and the arity pins also stayed green, as they must.
- Restored: blob back to `e0f74df` (equal to the HEAD blob), `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty, anchors back to 1 and 0.

## Clause-② re-derivation

Re-derived from the DELIVERED diff, not from the claim's prediction. `lowerDatasetCompareDateRange` is exported from its source module so the conformance runner can import it relatively, but `index.ts` re-exports a CLOSED named list from `./dataset-executor.js` that does not include it.

| read | my symbol | positive control `shiftRange` | negative control `lowerPreviewDateRange` |
|---|---|---|---|
| in `dist/index.d.ts` export statement | absent | present | absent |
| `Symbol in await import(entry)` | **false** | true | false |
| grep in `dist/index.js` | **2 hits** | 4 hits | 2 hits |

The third row is the point: the symbol IS in the bundle and is NOT reachable. A grep would have answered `yes`. The negative control is a symbol exported from its own source file, not re-exported by `index.ts`, and predating this diff — it proves the method distinguishes the two.

⇒ **Clause-②: no**, so the changeset is `patch`.

## Verification

Gate denominator, reconciled against `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran`, derived at `3a1d131fa`:

```
Run reconciliation — 62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 62 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 62 run,
  0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 62 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).
```

Four of the 62 first returned exit **3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`) or timed out (`check:query-options-erasure`). ⛔ Not read as green: the full workspace closure was built (`turbo run build`, 72/72 successful) and all four re-run to a real exit 0.

Tests:

- `@objectstack/service-analytics` full suite — **111 files, 2398 tests, 0 failures**.
- `@objectstack/rest` analytics door plus refusal envelope — **35 tests, 0 failures**. Run because the behaviour change is observable through the REST door; the first attempt failed on an unbuilt `dist`, which is a resolution error and not a red gate, so service-analytics was built and it was re-run to a real verdict.
- `@objectstack/service-analytics typecheck` — exit 0, and `tsc --listFiles` confirms the program really contains both the edited source and the edited test (1 and 1), with a negative control at 0.
- Lint, as a PROVEN narrowing: eslint over the 2 changed source files, **0 errors 0 warnings**, file count read from `--format json`. The invariance claim is read from eslint's own config — `eslint.config.mjs` sets no `parserOptions.project` and no typed rules, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run.

## Consumption-radius sweep

Swept by the RULE's consumers, not by the edited package. The changed rule is `runCompare`'s string-arm reading and its refusal envelope; its call chain is `DatasetExecutor.execute`, reached through `AnalyticsService.queryDataset`.

- `packages/services/service-analytics` — full suite green.
- `packages/rest` — the only other package that drives the executor; both analytics fixtures green.
- `packages/client` — SDK over a mocked transport, never runs the executor; no `compareTo` fixture.
- `examples/app-crm` — asserts widget metadata shape only, with `{current_quarter_start}` filter tokens rather than a `dateRange` preset; no executor run.
- `driver-memory` DST and timezone suites exercise the memory cube face, not this executor, and neither `@objectstack/core` nor driver-memory was touched.

## Acceptance notes

- `DatasetExecutor`'s compare math is UTC-calendar throughout (`parseUTC` reads a bare day as UTC midnight, `toISODate` emits a UTC day). For a non-UTC `selection.timezone` a preset's resolved bounds are therefore projected onto UTC day boundaries, which can make the comparison window a day longer than the org's own calendar would say. Pre-existing for the array arm and strictly better than the 400 it replaces, so ⛔ not widened into this PR.
